mission: Find working method to download Instagram reels/videos/posts from datacenter IP without login

verified_working_methods.name: embed_captioned_facebookexternalhit_ua
alternative_user_agents_that_also_work: Mozilla/5.0 (Linux; Android 10) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Instagram 250.0.0.20 Mobile Safari/537.36 Android
Mozilla/5.0 (iPhone; CPU iPhone OS 17_0 like Mac OS X) AppleWebKit/605.1.15 (KHTML, like Gecko) Mobile/15E148 Instagram 250.0.0.20
verified_working_methods.notes_on_ua: A plain Chrome browser UA returns a 200 with a login-wall shell (contextJSON is null/empty); the facebookexternalhit UA is the magic that makes Instagram return the SSR-embedded contextJSON with video_url. The Instagram-app UAs (Android/iOS) also work.
verified_working_methods.parse_strategy: Regex for \"video_url\":\"...\" inside contextJSON (stringified JSON value inside outer JSON). Decode JSON string escapes (\\/ -> /, \\u00253D -> =). Then the resulting https://scontent*.cdninstagram.com/.../*.mp4 URL is directly downloadable from CDN with any browser UA (no facebookexternalhit needed for the CDN download).
verified_working_methods.curl_example: UA='facebookexternalhit/1.1 (+http://www.facebook.com/externalhit_uatext.php)'; SC='DKw2J6TMZd7'; curl -s -L --max-time 20 -A "$UA" "https://www.instagram.com/p/$SC/embed/captioned/" -o page.html; python3 -c 'import re,json,sys; h=open("page.html").read(); m=re.search(r'\"contextJSON\":\"(.*?)\"(?=,\"[a-z])', h, re.DOTALL); raw=m.group(1); inner=json.loads("\""+raw+"\""); ctx=json.loads(inner); vu=[v for k,v in ctx["gql_data"]["shortcode_media"].items() if k=="video_url"][0]; print(vu.replace("\\\\/","/").replace("\\u00253D","="))' > video_url.txt; curl -s -L -A 'Mozilla/5.0' -o out.mp4 "$(cat video_url.txt)"

verified_working_methods.name: yt_dlp_with_facebookexternalhit_ua
verified_working_methods.notes_on_ua: yt-dlp's default Chrome UA hits Instagram's login wall from datacenter IPs (returns 'empty media response'). With --user-agent 'facebookexternalhit/1.1', yt-dlp internally hits the same SSR path and succeeds. This is the production-grade approach — well-maintained, format-merging (DASH video + audio), metadata-extracting.

verified_working_methods.name: socks5_residential_proxy_with_facebookexternalhit_ua
verified_working_methods.notes_on_ua: Optional fallback path. The direct method (Method 1/2) already works from datacenter IPs, so SOCKS5 is redundant. Tested as insurance: 2 of 15 sampled free public SOCKS5 proxies (from TheSpeedX/PROXY-List) successfully fetched the embed/captioned page and returned contextJSON with video_url. Production should not rely on free public SOCKS5 — use Method 1 or 2 directly.

production_recommendation.rationale: yt-dlp handles format selection (DASH video+audio merge), metadata, retries, atomic .part writes, and many edge cases already. Setting the facebookexternalhit UA unblocks the datacenter IP wall. Verified working on 4 different shortcodes, all producing valid MP4 files.
fallback_chain: 2. Direct curl to /embed/captioned/ + python regex for video_url + curl to CDN (no third-party deps, stdlib)
3. Same as 2 but with Instagram Android-app UA (works equally well)
4. Same as 2 but with Instagram iOS-app UA (works equally well)
5. SOCKS5 residential proxy + facebookexternalhit UA (insurance, not needed from datacenter IP per verified tests)
production_constraints_and_notes: CDN URLs (scontent-*.cdninstagram.com) expire within ~24h (token in &oe= param). Decode→download gap should be minutes.
facebookexternalhit UA is essential — plain browser UA gets blocked even on /embed/captioned/.
Method works for video posts and reels (GraphVideo in contextJSON.type). For image posts (GraphImage), use the same flow but extract display_url instead of video_url.
For carousel/sidecar posts (GraphSidecar), contextJSON contains an edge_sidecar_to_children array with multiple URLs.
The CDN download itself works with any UA — only the discovery (the /embed/captioned/ fetch) needs facebookexternalhit.
